item.title: Staying Logged In to Proxmox: Ticket Renewal, Expiry and Where API Tokens Stop
item.description: Back in 2023 I wrote up how go-proxmox logs in and ended it with a shrug: once a session existed the client never logged in again, so a ticket-based client died at the two hour mark and my advice was “use an API token for anything long running”. It took until this month to actually fix that properly, and it took three PRs from two of us to get there. Here’s the whole arc, plus the one place where an API token isn’t an option at all.

item.title: Logging In to Proxmox From Go: Tickets, CSRF Tokens and API Tokens
item.description: I just spent a week of evenings on the access side of go-proxmox: realms, groups, users and roles all landed, and before any of that I reworked how a client gets its credentials in the first place. Proxmox gives you two different ways to authenticate and they behave differently enough that it’s worth writing down how each one works on the wire and what the client does with it.
